name: Alpamayo trek to Laguna Jancarurish
region: Huascarán National Park, northern Cordillera Blanca
why: The first, wildest part of the Alpamayo circuit: from Hualcayán over two passes near 4,850 m to the glacier lake at the foot of Alpamayo, one of the most beautiful ice peaks in the world.
book: Huascarán National Park multi-day ticket (4-30 days: S/150 for foreigners in 2023). Hualcayán is reached by road from Caraz. Most go with an agency from Huaraz or Caraz with arrieros and donkeys; the full circuit continues east to Pomabamba.
water: Streams and lakes (treat them); carry 2 litres on the pass days.
dangers: Osoruri (about 4,860 m) and Vientunan (about 4,770 m) passes and camps above 4,200 m: acclimatise first.
Long remote days with no villages after Hualcayán and no rescue service.
Night frost; hail or snow on afternoons.
turnaround: Not over the Osoruri pass by 13:00: camp at Laguna Cullicocha and cross the next morning.

points.name: Hualcayán
points.note: Day 1: the village at about 3,100 m above Caraz. A long climb of some 1,500 m up the slope to the lake plateau.

points.name: Laguna Cullicocha
points.note: Camp near the dammed glacier lake at about 4,600 m, under Santa Cruz peak.

points.name: Osoruri pass
points.note: Day 2: about 4,860 m, then on over the Vientunan pass and down to the Los Cedros valley.

points.name: Jancarurish camp
points.note: The valley-floor camp at about 4,200 m in the Los Cedros valley, with Alpamayo's north side rising at its head.

points.name: Laguna Jancarurish, Alpamayo north base camp
points.note: Day 3: up the moraine to the turquoise glacier lake under Alpamayo and Jancarurish peak. A rest day here, then 2 days back.
